title: Cognition launches SWE-2 Flash — 3x faster, 5x cheaper, built on Inkling-Small
subtitle: The new coding model runs at roughly 200 tokens per second inside Devin and is free for paid subscribers through November 30, as Cognition targets high-volume agent work.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Cognition announced SWE-2 Flash on November 4 as a smaller, faster, cheaper sibling to its SWE-2 coding model. The company says Flash runs about three times faster and at one-fifth the price of SWE-2, with reports of roughly 200 tokens per second in practice. Architecturally, SWE-2 Flash is a 276-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 12 billion parameters active per token, fine-tuned from Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling-Small base. There is no public API and no public weights; access is through Devin Desktop and the Devin CLI, free for paid subscribers through November 30, 2026.

On benchmarks, Cognition claims SWE-2 Flash outperforms every American open-weight model on leading coding evaluations, including models roughly three times its size. Its comparison table shows Flash edging the larger SWE-2 on FrontierCode 2.0, while SWE-2 still leads on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE 1.1. The numbers come from Cognition's own evaluations and have not been independently verified — a caveat that applies to nearly every frontier-model launch this year.

The design choice here is telling. Rather than chase one more point of top-end quality, Cognition built a model tuned for the economics of agentic coding: many short, chained calls where latency and per-token cost dominate the bill. By picking Thinking Machines' Inkling-Small as the base, Cognition is also signaling that the US coding stack can now be assembled from multiple American labs' building blocks — not just the three frontier houses. The gated weight-sharing program Cognition mentioned, aimed at researchers and partners, is another small step back toward transparency in a product category that has been increasingly closed.

Takeaway for learners: a smaller, cheaper model shipped inside a working agent product beats a bigger model behind a paywall for most real tasks. When you benchmark any coding assistant, measure the dollars-per-finished-PR and the wait time on your actual repo — not the leaderboard score on a public benchmark the vendor also used to pick which numbers to publish.
